name: In Your Own Hand
tagline: People make their best things around you. So do you.
epigraph: 'Juice of A Few Flowers' sounds like a joke. The handwritten card says otherwise.
glassware: two nick-and-nora glasses (small, stemmed), chilled, each rim dipped in coarse sugar on the outside
language_row: Wren's Resonance on reading v4: ready. Her 4-gram check against every pour's reading is clean. Sibling echoes moved off: "the next time a" (*Instead*) → "when someone shows you"; "The only thing I added is" (*Fair Measure*) cut; the closing line's "say you made it" (the Craftsman's "say caraway") → "put your name on it" (Tomás, round 6). The he/him/his warnings in yours 1–4 are Gerald Murphy, and one "he drew" is Fitzgerald, never the guest (accepted by Wren, round 6). ✓
sources: Studio fact card `_studio/fact-cards/gerald-murphy.md`: Kathryn Price, "The 'Juice of a Few Flowers': Gerald and Sara Murphy's Life of Beautiful Things", *Gastronomica* 7:2 (2007), text and the photograph of his handwritten card (Gerald and Sara Murphy Papers, Beinecke, Yale; copy in `work/lover-creator/historian-murphy-recipe-card-gastronomica.jpg`), with the 15 February 1939 letter to Alexander Woollcott (its note 4) for the Bailey; Whitney Museum of American Art, *Cocktail* (1927), accession 95.188 (collection page). Drink: the card's measures; Gary Regan, *The Joy of Mixology* pdf 137 (sugar kept on the outside of the rim); *Flavor Matrix* grapefruit pdf 282 (consulted, set aside); Dave Arnold's style ranges via `balance.py`. Room notes: `work/lover-creator/`.
names_note: **In Your Own Hand**, the room's pick (all three, from round 4): the Muse's work, exact and under their own name, not someone else's version of them. Also considered: *Who's Asking* (Tomás withdrew it because it spends the ending's "since hardly anyone asks" twice), *Written Down*, *A Few Flowers*, *Two Glasses*.
open_items: **FLAG: balance is OUT on the sour ranges (strength, acid, sugar), and the room chose that.** 7.3% ABV, 10.92 g sugar/100 ml, 1.42% acid, ratio 7.7 (a sour's middle is 8.2). Tomás's proof (round 5, re-run by Hester): shaking, ice and the glass only add water, so Murphy's card fixes acid per ml of alcohol at 0.161–0.196, against at most 0.076 in any of Arnold's styles. Only changing one of his measures could bring it in range. The case, from all three: every OUT comes from his three-to-one hand, and pulling it into range would make the drink our idea of him, which is the Muse's own fear. It's the lightest and sharpest pour in the studio (of 30 specs, 2026-09-30: next lowest 8.8% ABV, next highest acid 0.98%). Robin's call: ship as it is, or ask the room to move a measure.

**The one change to his card is ours, and it's named:** ¾ oz of mint syrup. A syrup is forced, because sugar kept on the outside of the rim (Regan's method; the card says only "dip in coarse sugar") never reaches the drink. The mint comes from the Bailey, the cocktail he wrote he'd invented (1939 letter), and y4 owns the joining: "two of his recipes, and joining them is my idea". The plain rim-sugar syrup (same numbers) is kept as `mixologist-draft-card-alone-v2.md`.
**Serves 2:** his measures come to about 194 ml, so two nick-and-noras of about 97 ml each. The closing line builds on it.
**Grapefruit:** a guest note on the recipe row ("can interfere with some medicines: if you take any, check first"), backed by the CMAJ title; "statins" stays in Checks and is unsourced. Not a veto.

**Attribution:** "in Gerald's handwriting" rests on *Gastronomica*'s caption and its "copied out in his neat handwriting". The card is undated. "Invented by me" is said only of the Bailey, never of this glass.
**Crossings:** the syrup swapped three times (rounds 3–6) before Wren ruled on the files' state in round 7. Each voice's case is in the room record.

**Unverified, kept out:** Barry reusing the "few flowers" line, the Tomkins title, whether Booth's House of Lords is still made, and the father's bar tray (the Whitney and *Gastronomica* disagree). Library gap for Robin: Calvin Tomkins, *Living Well Is the Best Revenge* (fact card U1–U4).
